extra.message: The `username` query parameter is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 template string via `'Welcome ' + username + '!'` on line 14. User input is treated as template code, not as a template variable value. An attacker can inject arbitrary Jinja2 template expressions such as `{{ config }}` to leak sensitive application configuration, or more advanced payloads to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) via Jinja2 sandbox escapes (e.g., accessing `__globals__`, `os.popen`).

The rendered output containing user-supplied `username` is returned as `HTMLResponse(content=output)`. The `Environment()` created at line 12 has `autoescape=False` by default (no loader or autoescape config). Even discounting SSTI, an attacker can inject HTML/JavaScript payloads via the username parameter (e.g., `/?username=<script>alert('XSS')</script>`) which will be rendered unsanitized in the browser.

User-supplied `username` parameter is concatenated directly into the Jinja2 template string at line 14. The `from_string()` method treats this as raw template source, so an attacker can inject Jinja2 template syntax (e.g., `{{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}`) to achieve Server-Side Template Injection. This enables arbitrary Python code execution on the server.
